item.title: The de Sades Among Us
item.description: The seeds of evil that brought us Epstein, blatant censorship at the University of North Texas, the problem with wall labels, and a Black Medieval angel of love.

item.title: South Africa's Fiasco in Venice
item.description: South Africa withdraws from the Venice Biennale, Glenn Ligon and the color blue, and your guide to art in DC this spring.

item.title: Prisoners of Love: Until the Sun of Freedom
item.description: The only US presentation of this exhibition by renowned artists Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme is on view at The Bell Gallery, Brown University.

item.title: Detroit Institute of Arts Reinstalls African American Galleries at the Heart of the Museum
item.description: African American art history has often been underrepresented. “Reimagine African American Art” invites visitors to discover transformative works across two centuries.

item.title: Winter Storm Brings Art to a Halt in NYC
item.description: Museums across the city and the area will remain closed today.

item.title: Activists Hang Prince Andrew's Arrest Photo at the Louvre
item.description: The unflattering photo of the disgraced former royalty was taken after his arrest last week for his ties with sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Artists' Calendar Celebrates LA’s Everyday Landmarks
item.description: For 40 years, Nib Geebles and Abira Ali have chronicled the unspoken, day-to-day minutiae of their hometown in their beloved calendar.

item.title: How to Tell the Story of Extraction in Appalachia
item.description: Fia Backström explores this nexus of environmental degradation, disaster capitalism, and intergenerational poverty through embodied, compassionate, and durational research.

item.title: Chipping Away at the Facade of Mount Rushmore
item.description: In “Biography of a Mountain,” author Matthew Davis deftly weaves together interviews and stories that reveal so much more than a linear narrative of the monument’s history.

item.title: Reading a Biography of a Mountain
item.description: Mount Rushmore, originally known as Six Grandfathers, gets its own biography, plus Sarah Bond on museums’ approach to polychromy and whiteness.
